records.question: Choose the word that does not have the same vowel sound as the others
records.explanation: Shun, son and sun have /ʌ/ in standard British pronunciation; short has /ɔː/, so it is different.

records.question: Choose the word or phrase from A to D which has its meaning opposite to the underlined word or words in each sentence She was impertinent until she met her husband. Target: impertinent.
records.explanation: Impertinent means rudely disrespectful; courteous means polite and respectful, its contextual opposite.

records.question: Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s) Repugnant rules in the society should be repealed. Target: Repugnant.
records.explanation: Repugnant rules cause strong dislike or disgust; abhorrent has the same meaning in this context.

records.question: Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word The boss is quite inflexible once he has made up his mind. Target: inflexible.
records.explanation: An inflexible person will not change a settled position; unyielding expresses that firmness of will.

records.question: From the options lettered A-D, choose the option that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word. My mother is a shrewd businesswoman. Target: shrewd.
records.explanation: Shrewd means astute in practical judgement; gullible means easily deceived, the relevant opposite.

records.question: In the following question, choose the option that best completes the sentence. The guest would have arrived earlier but he was _______ in traffic.
records.explanation: Held up in traffic means delayed by traffic, explaining why the guest did not arrive earlier.

records.question: Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s) No one would complain if you emulate good behaviour Target: emulate.
records.explanation: To emulate good behaviour is to imitate it, usually with the intention of matching or improving on it.

records.question: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in bracket. Smoo[th] Target: th (bracketed in Smooth).
records.explanation: The bracketed th in smooth is voiced /ð/. Brother contains the same voiced consonant.

records.question: In each of the questions, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates.The union congratulated the ELECTED president.
choices: Did the union reject the elected president?
Did the union congratulate the elected chairman?
Did the management congratulate the elected president?
Did the union congratulate the ousted president?

observed_options.A: Did the union reject the elected president?
observed_options.B: Did the union congratulate the elected chairman?
observed_options.C: Did the management congratulate the elected president?
observed_options.D: Did the union congratulate the ousted president?

records.explanation: Stress on ELECTED contrasts the president with one who was ousted, while the union, action and office stay the same.

records.question: In each of the questions, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates.A good description INCLUDES specific nouns.
choices: Does a good description exclude specific nouns?
Does a good description include specific verbs?
Does a good description include obscure nouns?
Does a poor description include specific nouns?

observed_options.A: Does a good description exclude specific nouns?
observed_options.B: Does a good description include specific verbs?
observed_options.C: Does a good description include obscure nouns?
observed_options.D: Does a poor description include specific nouns?

records.explanation: Stress on INCLUDES contrasts inclusion with exclusion while preserving a good description and specific nouns.

records.question: Choose the word which has the same consonant sounds as the underlined letter(s) pleasure Target: s.
records.explanation: The underlined s in pleasure represents /ʒ/. Seizure contains that same voiced fricative.

records.question: In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. The solution lies in choosing between various negative alternatives.
choices: The solution lies in choosing between the positive and negative
The solution can be found in one of the negative options
The solution is a negative one

observed_options.B: The solution lies in choosing between the positive and negative
observed_options.C: The solution can be found in one of the negative options
observed_options.D: The solution is a negative one

records.explanation: Choosing between negative alternatives means finding the solution in one of those options, not adding a positive option.

records.question: In this question, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates. EMEKA finished his homework yesterday.
choices: Who finished his home work yesterday?
When did Emeka finish his home work?
Did Emeka do his home work yesterday?
Was Emeka helped to do his home work?

observed_options.A: Who finished his home work yesterday?
observed_options.B: When did Emeka finish his home work?
observed_options.C: Did Emeka do his home work yesterday?
observed_options.D: Was Emeka helped to do his home work?

records.explanation: Stress on EMEKA focuses the person who completed the homework; Who finished asks specifically for that person.

scope: Thirteen complete standalone selected publisher-labelled questions; remaining source inventory and prior duplicate/ambiguous dispositions retained privately.
